html:
China's first human spaceflight, launched on 15 October 2003. Yang Liwei, an air force pilot, orbited the Earth fourteen times in about 21 hours and landed in Inner Mongolia.

It made China the third country, after the Soviet Union and the United States, to put a person into orbit with its own rocket. That came 42 years after Yuri Gagarin and 46 years after Sputnik. The mission used a Long March rocket from the Jiuquan launch centre in the Gobi Desert, and a Shenzhou capsule based on the Soviet Soyuz design but built in China.

The flight was a source of national pride in the years of the Beijing Olympics and fast economic growth. China followed with spacewalks, a robot landing on the far side of the Moon in 2019 and its own Tiangong space station, finished in 2022.
